text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000009 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation, including on low-complexity patients, but the few documented 99215 claims all support the billed level, so the records are too thin to settle the question.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern because 99215 rates run several times the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include routine-looking diagnoses such as acute URI (C0003110, C0003224), follow-up visits (C0003291, C0003292) and unspecified abdominal pain (C0003112, C0003312), which would not usually call for high-complexity MDM. Against that, all 4 documented 99215 claims (for example C0003119 and C0003470) show high MDM and 50+ minutes. However, 4 charts is far too few to judge, and they may not be representative of the low-complexity 99215s. The one unsupported claim (C0003442) and the 2 no-lab notes are weak signals at most, though possible cloned or inflated documentation cannot be ruled out. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims listed above, then check whether those notes show genuine high-complexity MDM or template-like text."}
